title: Personal Credit Cards: counting the points still open on a card before an autopay source restoration
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: points still open on the card, for an autopay source restoration

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line. When rewards points on a card are used to bring the card's overdrawn autopay source checking account back to zero, it fixes how many points the card still holds, not yet used or removed.

## Rule

1. The count is taken from the card's own ledger at handling time.
2. Start from all points posted by the card's earning entries.
3. Take away all points posted by the card's redemption entries.
4. Take away all points posted by the card's forfeiture entries, which include removals that take back the points of a refunded purchase.
5. What remains is the number of points still open on the card.

## Worked example (hypothetical ledger)

| Ledger entries on the card | Points |
|---|---|
| earning entries, all together | 12000 |
| redemption entries, all together | 5000 |
| forfeiture entries, all together | 400 |
| points still open on the card | 12000 less 5000 less 400, that is 6600 |

## Points of judgement

- Every earning, redemption and forfeiture entry on the card's ledger counts, whatever its date.
- The figure comes from the ledger entries themselves at handling time; a points figure taken from anywhere else is not this count.
- Entries of another card of the same cardholder are not part of this card's count.
